set.approach: The trip starts at the Wallowa Lake trailhead, where the East Fork Wallowa River Trail (number 1804) climbs through forest, then meadows and beaver ponds, passing Rogers Lake before reaching Aneroid Lake roughly six miles in. Pete's Point sits above the lake between Tenderfoot Pass and Polaris Pass, and the route is the snow couloir on its north face. Carry an ice axe for the couloir; rockfall is possible.

review.notes: MP: 6 miles to Aneroid Lake, Pete's Point between Tenderfoot and Polaris, north-face couloir, rockfall. Oregon Hikers: trail 1804, Rogers Lake, Aneroid about six miles. No descent source.

set.descent_text: From the top of the gully there are two ways down: downclimb the gully itself, or hike across the crater rim and downclimb the neighbouring Eleven O'clock Gully, whichever looks easier on the day. Either gully needs solid snow cover to be in condition, and a cornice may cap the top of this one, so look it over from below before committing. Those continuing to the summit can cross the west face and join the Northwest Ridge.

review.notes: Both MP pages in Broken Top's Crook cirque; Nine O'clock page gives the descent options; Eleven O'clock says downclimb the route and avoid it without consolidated snow. Single-page origin so medium. No approach source.

set.approach: Start at the Pioneer Gulch trailhead and follow the Pioneer Gulch Trail until it meets the Diamond Peak Trail. Leave the trail there and head straight uphill, trending toward climber's left, until you reach the southwest ridge. In winter, with the Summit Lake road shut, this is the easiest line to reach.

review.notes: Single MP page; distance/gain (7.5 mi, 4000 ft) omitted because only one source readable. No descent source.

set.approach: The headwall lies to the right of the Wy'East face as seen from below, so parties reach it the way they reach that route. One option is from Timberline up the White River Glacier; the other is directly from the Mt Hood Meadows ski area up the Newton Clark Glacier. Bring pickets, ice axe, crampons and a helmet for the glacier approach and the steep headwall above.

review.notes: Single MP page. No descent source (only a warning about hidden cliffs when descending the headwall).

set.approach: From the trailhead parking lot a good trail runs about a mile to the first Pacific Crest Trail junction. Stay on the McLoughlin climbers trail, go straight past a second PCT junction that leads north, and follow smooth trail for a few miles before the footing turns rocky, with large step-ups. The well-worn trail leads to the East Ridge itself, and the final slope to the pointed summit is scree or snow.

review.notes: Single MP page; counts left approximate. No descent source readable.

set.approach: Start at Cloud Cap, on Hood's north flank, and follow the Timberline Trail to the moraine, then continue toward Cooper Spur until you reach a large cairn. From the cairn a climbers trail descends onto the Eliot Glacier; walk across it toward the Snow Dome, which marks the start of the climbing. When the road to Cloud Cap is closed, the Tilly Jane trail is the way in and the approach is longer.

review.notes: MP Sunshine page for the walk; MP Cooper Spur page names Tilly Jane and Cloud Cap as the two starts. No descent source for this route.

set.approach: Begin at Timberline Lodge and take the marked climbers trail that runs up beside the ski area's right boundary, staying out from under the lifts. Head up toward Crater Rock, as for the standard south side route, but go around the west side of the rock rather than the east side where most parties go. The route starts as a diagonal ascent toward the western crater rim. Avalanche terrain is common here, so cross the rim before the sun warms the slope.

review.notes: WCR page: leaves below Crater Rock, west side; avalanche warning. South Side page: Timberline Lodge start, trail along right edge of ski area. No descent source.

set.approach: Drive to the Green Lakes trailhead on the Cascade Lakes Highway and hike in to the Green Lakes basin, where parties often camp. From the northern end of the basin, turn uphill by a gully to reach the Prouty Glacier. Crampons and an ice axe are needed when there is snow, and a rope and pickets for a possible bergschrund below the rock band.

review.notes: Single MP page. No descent source.

set.descent_text: Descend the way you came, down the South Sister Climbers Trail to the Devils Lake trailhead. The upper trail is loose volcanic scree and cinder that slides underfoot, and with snow cover an ice axe and crampons may be needed. Parties who loop through Moraine Lake instead face a steep, slippery trail into the canyon, with a rugged first stretch that needs hands.
set.approach: Start at the Devils Lake trailhead on the Cascade Lakes Highway and take the signed South Sister Climbers Trail, filling out the self-issued wilderness permit at the start. The trail crosses a footbridge over Tyee Creek, crosses the highway and climbs steeply through hemlock forest to a sandy plateau, where you go straight at the four-way junction. It passes the Moraine Lake valley and continues over loose cinder to a sandy saddle at the Lewis Glacier moraine. The round trip is roughly 11 to 12 miles.

review.notes: inlandnwroutes: trailhead, trail, landmarks, ~11 mi, Moraine Lake loop descent. MP: 12.5 mi, self-issue permit, scree, axe/crampons if snow. Descent = return route (both imply).

or_middle_sister_southeast_ridge.skip_reason: Only source is a one-line route page (walk-up from the Chambers Lakes area); no trailhead, approach or descent text to support a paragraph.

or_mt_jefferson_north_ridge.skip_reason: Only source says the ridge is gained from a Jefferson Park camp and gives no trailhead or descent; the neighbouring glacier route page advises against descending this ridge, and no source says how parties get down from the top.
